In summary, our research is concerned with
the classical capacity of quantum channels with general Markovian correlated noises.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the capacity of a channel with Markovian correlated quantum noise is equal to the capacity of an equivalent channel with uncorrelated classical noise.
for a channel with Markovian correlated memory, the classical capacity can be computed by means of the communicating classes and the invariant measure of the Markovian chain.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in general, the classical capacity of a noisy quantum communication channel is determined by the structure of the noise process, and the classical capacity is not determined solely by the quantum channel.
the classical capacity of a Markovian channel can be evaluated in the same way as the capacity of a memoryless channel.
, for a channel with Markovian noise, the channel is either forgetful or non-forgetful, and the corresponding capacities are given by our main results.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the classical capacity of a channel with general Markovian correlated memory is given by a sum of the capacities of the communicating classes, each with its own memory.
, in the general case, it is possible to evaluate the capacity of the channel without knowing the exact form of the Markovian noise.
for a quantum channel with long-term correlated noise, the capacity depends only on the communicating classes of its Markov chain and not on the details of the channel itself.
